newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia concerned at press curbs in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Russia concerned at press curbs in Belarus.

text.p: Russia expressed concern on Tuesday about problems facing Russian journalists in Belarus, one of Moscow's closest allies, and urged Minsk to guarantee media freedom.
But Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky also urged Russian reporters, some of whom have been stopped by the Belarus authorities from filing stories, to operate within the law.
"The very fact that Russian television channels have been denied the right to send information materials from Minsk prompts deep concern in the Kremlin," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.

Belarus authorities began cracking down on foreign television broadcasters on Sunday, stopping journalists from entering the main television centre from where they usually transmit coverage of the former Soviet republic.

"We have the right to expect that the principles of freedom of information will be restored in full and that Russian journalists will get the possibility to fulfil their professional duties without obstacles," Yastrzhembsky said.
"At the same time, we call on Russian mass media, accredited in Belarus, to act in a sovereign state within the law, to preserve the rules of objectivity and lack of bias," he said.
